entries.context: Button on an EMPTY chair in the four-seat lobby roster. Opens the Roblox invite sheet. Very tight fixed-width chip, so keep it to one short word plus the plus sign.

Status line under a player's name in the lobby roster, meaning they have pressed Ready. Lower case on purpose: it sits under the name as a caption, not as a heading. Keep it short, the chip is fixed width.
Name shown on a lobby chair occupied by a computer-controlled chef rather than a person. A noun, the kind of player it is.

The main lobby button WHEN OTHER PEOPLE ARE PRESENT. It is a pledge -- 'I am ready, start when everyone else is' -- not a command to begin. When the player is alone the button says START SHIFT instead (ui.start_shift), because then it really does start the round. NOTE: ui.ready is a DIFFERENT string, 'READY!' with an exclamation mark, still used on the Kitchen Card. This one has no exclamation mark because it alternates with START SHIFT on the same button and they should be punctuated alike.
Button at the end of a shift that opens the device's share sheet with a screenshot of the crew. 'Photo' as in a picture of the team, not a photograph in general.

entries.context: Status under a player's name on a lobby chair when they have stopped responding and the crew can start without them. Lower case caption on a fixed-width chip; keep it to one short word.

Status under a player's name on a lobby chair when they are present but have not pressed Ready yet -- deciding, browsing the wardrobe, not gone. Lower case caption on a fixed-width chip; keep it short.

Caption on the lobby chair the local player is sitting in. The chair's headline is the CHARACTER (Bramble, Pip, Nori, Mochi); this line says who is in it, and for yourself that is simply 'you'. Lower case, fixed-width chip.
Caption on your own lobby chair once you have pressed Ready. Same line as ui.chair_you with the readiness added. Keep it short; the chip is fixed width.

Caption on a lobby chair a computer-controlled chef is filling. Two parts either side of a middle dot: what is in the chair, and the offer -- tapping the chair makes YOU play that character instead and the bot takes the one you left. Lower case, fixed-width chip.

tr.ja: ボット・タップで交代

entries.context: Caption on a lobby chair nobody is in -- no player and no bot. Same shape as ui.chair_bot: the state, then the offer. A separate + button in the corner invites somebody into it instead.

note: Bare language codes, not region locales. The experience registers its languages as languageCodeType=Language (en, fr, de, id, ja, ko, pt, es) and the dashboard importer rejects de-de/id-id/ja-jp/ko-kr against that. Bare codes are also the better runtime choice: Roblox falls back from a player's region locale (ja-jp) to the base language (ja), so one column covers every region of that language.
